newsitem.title: USA: IRAQ OIL FLOW SCARES U.S. CASH CRUDE PRICES LOWER.
newsitem.headline: IRAQ OIL FLOW SCARES U.S. CASH CRUDE PRICES LOWER.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices slid lower Wednesday, deflated by the realization the clock is ticking ever-closer for resumption of Iraqi oil sales under a renewed "oil-for-food" accord with the U.N.

Outright benchmark prices drifted steadily lower as the session progressed, leaving September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing some 35 cents weaker to $20.40-50 a barrel. September/October rolls steadied at -11/8 cents, putting WTI/Cushing Postings Plus around $1.93-95.
Iraq can begin submitting oil sales contracts to U.N. overseers late Friday morning, barring objections from members of the U.N. Security Council Sanctions Committee.

Iraqi exports could then begin as soon as this weekend, and would likely start to hit markets by late next week. Earlier Wednesday, Iraqi oil minister Amir Muhammed Rasheed said Baghdad expected to export the full $2 billion worth of oil allowed by the accord.
The Iraq developments offset continued supply concerns in Colombia, where exports have been hindered after rebel pipeline bombings, and at the Venezeulan PDVSA refinery in Curacao.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James sweet grade barrels recovered from morning declines to end at a 17-18 cents premium to the September benchmark.
LLS sold in the morning from highs at 21 cents over WTI, to lows at only 13 cents above the benchmark.
Traders said weak Dated Brent and Brent CFD's hurt the LLS in the morning.
"It was really driven down early, but by the end of the day it was back, and was still relatively cheap when compared to bringing over Brent," said a cash dealer in the Gulf.
Other grade barrels selling on Wednesday included Midland/WTI at 31 and 30 cents under the marker, and West Texas Sour/Midland at $1.50 and $1.48 below WTI.
